window: Mina: On May 2 I bought my sister Nora a yellow dress for 48 dollars for her birthday. Please remember what I gave her.
why: One event must keep recipient, item, color, amount and date rather than only a general caring trait.

window: Mina：9月12日我在青禾书店买了《长日将尽》，花了68元，是送给姐姐Nora的生日礼物。帮我记住买的是哪本书和价格。
why: Chinese capture preserves the book title, store, amount, recipient and date.

window:
Mina: Hello!
Aster: Hi!
Mina: Thanks, have a nice day.
Aster: You too!
why: Keeping specifics must not turn pure pleasantries into memory cards.

window:
Aster: You could buy Nora a yellow dress from Cedar Shop for 48 dollars.
Mina: That is just your suggestion, not something I have bought or decided to do. I have nothing else to add.
why: An unaccepted assistant suggestion must not become a person's purchase or plan.

window: Mina: I said the ticket for the play Glass Harbor cost 72 dollars, but I read the receipt wrong. It actually cost 27 dollars. Please remember the correction.
why: A correction keeps the corrected value; human review must verify 72 is not presented as the current price.

cards.content: Mina bought her sister Nora a yellow dress at Cedar Shop on May 2 for 48 dollars.

cards.summary: Delivery of the same birthday gift
cards.content: Mina gave that same yellow dress to Nora on May 5, wrapped in a blue box. Nora wore it to dinner at Lake Cafe.

why: Merging a purchase and delivery of the same gift must preserve every source-specific value, not just the birthday theme.

cards.content: Mina于9月12日从成都搬到上海，搬家公司是青禾搬家，费用1800元，用了6小时。

window: Mina：补充一下9月12日那次搬家，最后一箱书是晚上8点送到的。请把这个也记在那次搬家里。
why: Thickening adds delivery time without erasing the original cities, mover, cost, duration or date.
